items.title: A good compilation of footage showing how the overnight and early morning attack on the Moscow region unfolded, including moments of impact. #Russia
items.summary:
A good compilation of footage showing how the overnight and early morning attack on the Moscow region unfolded, including moments of impact. #Russia
Video
NOELREPORTS 🇪🇺 🇺🇦 (@NOELreports)
Quite a night in Moscow and the surrounding region:
Ukraine threw a broad mix of systems into the attack: FP-1, RZ-100, MICH-2000, Palianytsia, Vendetta, Liutyi, Bars, Flamingo, Sichen and Pelican. One correction from earlier: Pelican is a fixed-wing drone, not the FP-7 ballistic missile as initially assumed.
According to our information, the Moscow Refinery took six hits. A logistics warehouse in Sofyino was hit and burned down completely, another undisclosed facility near Moscow was struck, and explosions and fires were reported at CHPP-22 near Lyubertsy. Reportedly, 6-8 Flamingo missiles were launched, with all intercepted before reaching Moscow. One came within about 20 km of the city. Russia even scrambled an A-50 AEW&C aircraft to hunt incoming cruise missiles and high-speed drones. Russia claimed 1,110 Ukrainian UAVs were downed, a figure we remain skeptical about.
— http://shitter.thepixora.com/NOELreports/status/2101708266862526862#m

items.title: "As Russian attacks on Ukraine's businesses escalate, the government's push to attract investment to Ukraine's wartime economy is coming up against a more immediate challenge: keeping businesses alive at all... The last month has been grueling for Ukraine’s businesses, particularly in and around the capital, as Russia launches waves of daytime drone attacks to throttle Ukraine’s economy. This year alone, businesses are expected to lose a staggering $10 billion, according to the Economy Ministry... One of the major issues for companies has been access to war-risk insurance. While big international players, like Coca-Cola, are able to afford coverage, the premiums are simply too high and insufficient for 94% of companies in Ukraine, according to a survey by the European Business Association. In response, the government is working on a new compensation fund to cover up to $10 million in "first losses," while the remainder will be covered by insurers." https://kyivindependent.com/as-russia-targets-ukraines-economy-keeping-businesses-alive-takes-priority/
